name: Harvify Stock Manager
author: harv

sections.description:
Harvify Stock Manager gives you a single, fast dashboard to manage WooCommerce inventory without opening product pages one by one. Filter your catalogue, edit stock, price, SKU and status inline, expand variable products to edit each variation, and save everything at once.

Free features:

  • Single-screen stock table for every product and variation
  • Inline edit: stock quantity, stock status, manage-stock, backorders,
    SKU, price, sale price, weight, tax status, tax class, shipping class — save
    per row or all at once
  • Filter by category, product type and stock status; search by name or SKU; sort
  • Show/hide columns
  • Low-stock and out-of-stock quick views
  • CSV import and export of your stock data
  • Basic stock log of recent changes made in the manager
  • WooCommerce HPOS compatible

Pro features (Harvify Pro Bundle):

  • Back-in-stock notifications — a “notify me when available” form on
    out-of-stock product pages; subscribers are emailed automatically when you
    restock
  • Low-stock alerts — to the store owner via email, Slack, Discord, Telegram
    or a generic webhook
  • Per-product and per-category low-stock thresholds (beyond WooCommerce’s
    single global threshold)
  • Full audit history — every stock change from every source (manager edits
    and order-driven) with old→new, source and user, filterable and CSV-exportable
  • Scheduling — a recurring low-stock digest email and a recurring stock CSV
    emailed to you
  • Auto out-of-stock — stock-managed products that hit zero are taken off
    sale automatically, on a schedule and the moment a quantity changes, so a
    CSV import or a supplier sync cannot leave a sold-out product on sale.
    Backorder products are left alone, and every change is written to the stock
    log
  • Bulk-by-filter — set, increase, decrease or change stock status across
    every product matching your current filter (with a stock-status filter, only
    the products and variations that match it are changed)
  • Stock insights — total stock value and units, status counts, and your
    most/least stocked products

Editing your stock

  1. Go to Harvify → Stock Manager. The Stock tab lists every product.
  2. Narrow the list with the category, product type and stock-status filters, or
    type in Search product…. The Low stock and Out of stock views show
    what needs attention.
  3. Click into any cell to change it — stock quantity, status, price, SKU and the
    rest. Open the + next to a variable product to edit each variation.
  4. Click Save changes to save every edited row at once, or Discard to drop
    the edits.
  5. Use Columns ▾ to choose which columns you see; the choice is remembered in
    your browser.

Import CSV and Export CSV move your stock data in and out as a
spreadsheet. The Stock log tab lists the recent changes made here.

External services

This plugin connects to Freemius, the licensing and update service Harvify uses to
sell and deliver the Pro tier of its plugins.

Nothing is sent to Freemius unless you choose to send it. On activation you are shown
Freemius’s standard opt-in screen. Until you answer it a fresh install makes no
outbound request at all, and if you choose Skip the free tier stays fully usable
and still sends nothing. Data is transmitted only when you take one of these
actions:

  • You click “Allow & Continue” on the Freemius opt-in screen. This sends your
    site address, your administrator email address, and your WordPress, PHP and active
    plugin/theme details, so Harvify can provide support and know which environments to
    test against. Skipping that screen sends nothing and leaves the plugin working
    normally.
  • You enter a Pro Bundle licence key. This sends the key together with your site
    address so the licence can be activated for that site. While a licence is active the
    site also re-checks periodically that it is still valid and whether a Pro update is
    available.

Service provided by Freemius, Inc. – https://freemius.com/
Terms of service: https://freemius.com/terms/
Privacy policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/harvify-stock-manager/
  2. Activate via Plugins → Installed Plugins
  3. Go to Harvify → Stock Manager
  4. Ensure WooCommerce is active
sections.faq:
Can I edit variation stock?

Yes. Variable products show a “+” expander in the table; open it to inline-edit each variation’s stock, price and status.

Are back-in-stock emails consent-based?

Yes. Shoppers explicitly enter their email in the opt-in form on an out-of-stock product. When you restock, they’re emailed once and the list is cleared.

Do low-stock alerts spam me?

No. An alert fires only when a product first crosses at or below its threshold, and re-arms once stock recovers above it.

Where is stock data stored?

Stock lives in WooCommerce’s own product data — Harvify Stock Manager just reads and writes it through WooCommerce, so it stays compatible with HPOS and the rest of your store.
sections.changelog:
1.0.19

  • Requires WordPress 6.2 or later: reading the catalogue a page at a time uses a WordPress 6.1
    feature to release each page from memory.

1.0.18

  • Fixed: on a large catalogue the CSV export could run out of memory. It read every
    product at once and built the whole file before sending any of it. It now reads products
    a hundred at a time and writes each row as it goes, so its memory use stays the same however
    many products the shop has. Rows come in product-ID order.

1.0.17

  • Fixed: the Columns button. The column choices were always open and the button did
    nothing; they are now tucked away until you press Columns, and stay open while you tick.
  • Fixed: the stock log names a variation by its product and size (“Tee — S”), not the size
    alone, and shows fields and choices in the table’s words (“Stock”, “Out of stock”).

1.0.16

  • Fixed: the Low stock card counted every product in stock. It now counts the products and
    variations at or below WooCommerce’s low-stock threshold, and clicking it lists them.
  • Fixed: variations are in the counts and the views. A variable product with a sold-out size
    is counted under Out of stock and listed when you click the card or filter by stock status,
    and the SKU box finds a variation by its own SKU.
  • Fixed: sorting by SKU and by stock. Sorting by SKU sorted by date; sorting by stock put
    products whose stock is not counted among the ones at 0. They now sort as labelled, with
    products that have no SKU or no counted stock last.
  • New: save one row on its own. Each row has a Save button beside the page-wide Save
    changes.
  • Fixed: a save says what WooCommerce did not keep. A SKU another product already has, a
    sale price at or above the price, a stock status on a product whose stock is counted, a
    quantity on a product whose stock is not, renaming a variation, and a value that is not one of
    the choices are now refused with the reason, and the field stays marked on screen. They were
    reported as “1 product(s) updated.” Nothing refused is written or logged.
  • Fixed: the dashboard cards update after a save without reloading the page.
  • Fixed: CSV. Importing an unchanged export changes nothing (variation names were exported
    as their attributes); the export carries tax class and shipping class; a semicolon- or
    tab-separated file (as Excel saves in much of Europe) is read; a file with no id or sku column
    is refused with the reason; and the import reply names each skipped row and why.
  • New: a Settings tab on the free version, with the low-stock threshold the cards count
    against and the “delete data when this plugin is deleted” control, which until now was on no
    screen you could reach.

1.0.15

  • Fixed: on a site running only this plugin, the Upgrade tab and the Plan screen now show
    what the free version includes and what a licence adds.     They showed a single line: the
    plugin shipped the feature catalogue but did not load it, so it only worked where another
    Harvify plugin was also active.

1.0.14

  • Internal names now start with harvify_stock_ instead of hsm_, as
    WordPress.org requires. Your settings, stock log, audit history, per-product
    thresholds, back-in-stock subscriber lists and scheduled jobs are carried across
    automatically on the first page load after updating; nothing needs doing.
  • Freemius now asks before connecting. On activation you see Freemius’s standard
    opt-in screen with a Skip button; skipping sends nothing and the plugin works as
    before. The External services section is updated to match.
  • Fixed: “delete data on uninstall” left most of the data behind. It removed the
    stock log and one setting, but not the alert, schedule, audit and threshold
    settings or the per-product data. It now removes everything the plugin stores.
  • Readme: step-by-step instructions for editing stock.

1.0.13

  • Added: a single Support entry in the Harvify menu, so you can reach us from
    inside WordPress. Until now no plugin offered a contact route at all. One entry for
    the whole suite rather than one per plugin.
  • No behaviour changes.

1.0.12

  • Added: an External services section to this readme, naming every third-party
    service the plugin can contact, exactly what is sent, when, and each provider’s terms
    and privacy policy. Required for WordPress.org submission.
  • Changed: the Contributors field now names the correct WordPress.org account.
  • No behaviour changes.

1.0.11

  • Fixed: deactivating the plugin now cancels the low-stock digest, the scheduled
    export and the automatic out-of-stock sweep. The plugin had no deactivation
    routine at all, so all three stayed queued.

1.0.10

  • Docs: the readme documents all five screenshots. It listed four while five ship,
    which renders as an empty frame on the plugin directory listing.

1.0.9

  • Added: a single Manage licence link on the Plan screen, so an active customer can
    deactivate this site, change their licence key or re-check their licence without
    needing a URL from support. No per-plugin Account tab is added.

1.0.8

  • One upgrade link instead of one per plugin. With several Harvify plugins active the
    menu showed a row called “Upgrade” for each of them, all identically labelled, and it kept
    saying Upgrade to people who had already bought. They are replaced by a single Plan
    screen that says what the bundle costs, what it covers, and whether your licence is active.
  • The dashboard is quiet again. Each plugin used to add its own “opt in to make this
    better” notice to the main WordPress dashboard, so five plugins meant five notices. Harvify
    plugins now share one queue: promotional notices appear only on Harvify’s own screens, and
    only one at a time. Licence and account messages are never held back.
  • Fixed: the “Data & uninstall” box covered the page. It was being drawn into the admin
    footer, which WordPress pins to the bottom of the screen, so it floated on top of whatever was
    underneath it. It now sits in the page like any other card. Saving it also tells you what it
    saved, instead of just reloading.
  • Fixed: the upgrade screen advertised the wrong number of sites. Several plugins listed
    the Freelancer and Agency plans as covering 5 and 25 sites. They cover 3 and 10.

1.0.7

  • The “delete my data on uninstall” setting had no way to be switched on. The plugin read an
    option that nothing in the interface ever wrote, so the cleanup it guarded could never run. It
    is now a real control on the plugin’s own screen, still defaulting to off.

1.0.6

  • Fixed: the branded admin header and cards were completely unstyled. The shared design
    system is scoped to a CSS class the app never applied, so the header and card chrome
    rendered as plain text instead of the Harvify admin design used by the rest of the suite.
  • Fixed: the Free/Pro badge in the header never appeared. The plan pill was passed to the
    shared admin header under the wrong key, so nothing on screen said which tier you were on.
  • Fixed: the “Upgrade to Pro Bundle” button went nowhere — built with the wrong argument
    names, so the link fell back to “#”, the Pro feature list was dropped, and no “Compare plans”
    link rendered.
  • The Upgrade screen now states what the free tier keeps (the stock table for every product and
    variation, inline editing, filters, quick views, CSV import/export and the basic log) before
    listing what Pro adds.

1.0.5

  • The back-in-stock email is now a proper HTML email, matching the Harvify Wishlist reminder
    it is a sibling of — store header, product name and price, and a real button instead of a bare
    URL. The fix that stops product names arriving as “Kettle & Co” is preserved: the name
    is decoded and then escaped for HTML, so it reads correctly either way.
  • Pro features now stop when a licence lapses rather than continuing on the installed premium
    build: back-in-stock notifications, low-stock alerts, the audit history, scheduling, bulk edits,
    insights and per-product thresholds. Thresholds fall back to WooCommerce’s own global setting.
  • A lapse never destroys anything. In particular, restocking while lapsed no longer consumes
    the back-in-stock waiting list: nobody is emailed, and nobody is silently dropped either — every
    shopper who was waiting still gets their email on the first restock after renewal.

1.0.4

  • Fixed (Pro): product names with an “&” reached customers as “&”. The back-in-stock
    email is plain text, and it carried the product title exactly as WordPress stores it.
    WordPress encodes a title on save for any role WITHOUT the unfiltered_html capability —
    and Shop Manager, the role WooCommerce creates for the people who manage products, does not
    have it. So a shop manager saving “Kettle & Co” stored “Kettle & Co”, and the shopper’s
    email read “Back in stock: Kettle & Co”. It was never spotted because test products
    were made by an administrator, who does keep the bare “&”. The same fix is applied to the
    two other plain-text messages that carried a product name: the low-stock alert (email,
    Slack, Discord, Telegram and webhook alike) and the low-stock digest.

1.0.3

  • New (Pro): auto-set out-of-stock. Stock-managed products whose quantity is zero are marked out of
    stock automatically — on the schedule you choose, and immediately whenever WooCommerce reports a
    quantity change. It also puts products back in stock when the quantity rises again, which you can turn
    off separately.
  • Products that accept backorders are never touched: they are meant to sell at zero.
  • Every automatic change is written to the stock log (and the Pro audit trail) with its old and new value,
    so nothing changes your catalogue silently.

1.0.2

  • Added the two inline-edit fields that were missing: tax class and shipping class. The
    stock table promised eleven editable fields and offered nine — tax status was there, tax
    class and shipping class were not. Both are now editable per row and with Save all, with the
    choices read from the classes your shop actually has.

1.0.1

  • Your licence is now manageable from the plugin itself. The Account screen was previously
    hidden, which also hid Deactivate License — so a licence could not be released from one
    site to move it to another without contacting support. It is visible again, along with the
    licence key, plan, Sync and Change License.
  • Harvify → Tools now opens with a Your licences table: every installed Harvify plugin,
    the plan it is on, whether Pro features are actually running, and a link to its Account screen.
    Freemius gives each product its own separate Account page, so this is the one place that
    answers “what am I on” across the whole bundle.
  • The repeated “Opt in to make … better!” admin notice no longer appears. Licence, plan and
    update notices are unaffected — only the opt-in prompt is suppressed.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: single-screen inline stock editor (products + variations), filters, column control, low/out-of-stock views, CSV import/export and a basic stock log.
  • Pro: back-in-stock customer notifications, low-stock owner alerts (email + Slack/Discord/Telegram/webhook), per-product/category thresholds, full audit history, scheduling, bulk-by-filter and stock insights.

short_description: Inline-edit WooCommerce stock, price and status for every product and variation from one screen — filter, bulk-save and CSV import/export.
